samples.source: genius.md: Three-Act Gravitational Field + The Curse + War of Art (Resistance)
samples.title: Pressfield Pitch Bible — The Forge (1-Hour Drama)
samples.notes: Demonstrates Pressfield's Three-Act Gravitational Field, The Curse (character flaw driving narrative), and Resistance as invisible antagonist. Expert-level because the professional world literally embodies the thematic arc—demolitions expert learning to build.

samples.source: genius.md: Newspaper Economy + Outsider Lens + Procedural Detail as Character
samples.title: Connelly Cold Open — Fault Lines Episode 1
samples.notes: Demonstrates Connelly's Newspaper Economy (dialogue cut to bone), Outsider Lens (detective who notices what doesn't matter), and procedural detail as character revelation. Expert-level because every object (the coffee, the door scratch, the trash can) does psychological work without the writer announcing it.

samples.title: Pressfield Logline Construction — Four Genre Exemplars
samples.notes: Demonstrates GP2 (Future-Flash), GP3 (Start at End), GP4 (Genre Spin), GP5 (Curse), GP6 (Hero Changes), GP7 (Sacrifice), GP8 (Extraordinary World), GP14 (Badge), GP18 (Child). Includes anti-exemplar with full physics diagnosis and Five-Force test.

samples.title: The Quiet Interview — Dialogue Scene with Craft Diagnosis
samples.notes: Demonstrates Newspaper Economy (dialogue cut in half), Subtext Architecture (nothing said directly), Power Through Restraint, Character-Specific Cadence. 267 words, zero adverbs, body language carries all emotion. The vending machine functions as compressed emotional arc.

samples.title: Hawley — Season Architecture & The Withheld Payoff
samples.notes: Theme-first breaking, ending-first, the moral mirror (engineer desire then indict it), and score-where-music-doesn't-go. Expert-level: the architecture is total for the writer and invisible to the audience; the genre payoff is refused and inverted so meaning arrives through restraint.
